Old patterns, new clothes.

An outdoor fashion show in Guangxi brought an old craft into modern life. Forty sets of clothes used traditional Zhuang patterns. The show took place among green valleys and waterfalls. Li Cunling, a craft worker from Jingxi, helped create it.

Zhuang brocade is a kind of cloth with colorful patterns woven into it. It often uses bright red, yellow, blue and green. The patterns can include frogs, flowers and diamond shapes. In the past, families used the cloth for clothes, bed covers and things for carrying babies.

Li has worked on this craft for more than thirty years. She wants to protect its traditions while finding new ways to use them. The modern clothes show how patterns from the past can become part of what people wear today.
